relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: Armstrong began his teaching career in 1936 at University College, Swansea, Wales. His tenure at the university lasted until 1939.

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: He then began teaching at the Royal University of Malta in Valletta as a professor of classics. In 1943, he became a classical sixth form master at Beaumont College

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: In 1943, he became a classical sixth form master at Beaumont College, Old Windsor, Berkshire, England. Three years later, in 1946, he relocated to Cardiff University

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: Three years later, in 1946, he relocated to Cardiff University to take up the position of lecturer in Latin. From 1950 to 1972 he served as the Gladstone Professor of Greek at University of Liverpool

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: From 1950 to 1972 he served as the Gladstone Professor of Greek at University of Liverpool in Liverpool, England, being appointed professor emeritus upon retirement in 1972.

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: From 1970 to 1971, Armstrong was a Killam Senior Fellow at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada.

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.role: visiting professorship of classics and philosophy
relations.evidence: He held a visiting professorship of classics and philosophy at the university from 1972.

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: He was also named a visiting professor at Manhattanville College in 1966.

relations.subject: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
relations.evidence: He was a founding editor of Dionysius, together with J. A. Doull and R. D. Crouse.
